subject.title: RFC: policy on agent-directed instruction content in docs

question: Should ClawHub publish a standalone agent-directed-instruction policy now, or fold its acceptability line and examples into the broader content-policy RFC before implementation?
rationale: The remaining work selects the public trust boundary, its owner, its relationship to declared capabilities, and the handling of borderline legitimate instructions; existing moderation infrastructure cannot safely infer those choices.

options.title: Fold into content policy
options.body: Make this issue’s examples and boundary a dedicated section of the broader content-policy RFC, then publish one coherent policy and internal rationale.

options.title: Publish a focused policy first
options.body: Land a narrow documentation-instruction guideline now, with an explicit follow-up to reconcile enforcement and manifest questions in the broader RFC.

options.title: Keep it reviewer-only
options.body: Retain the boundary as internal moderation guidance until public wording and appeals ownership are agreed.

recommendation.title: Fold into content policy
recommendation.body: Make this issue’s examples and boundary a dedicated section of the broader content-policy RFC, then publish one coherent policy and internal rationale.

likelyOwner.reason: Their active collaborator-authored RFC already owns the broader public content-policy distinction this issue needs to resolve.
